headline: Towhid Hridoy hits maiden Test century to lead Bangladesh fightback
summary: The 24-year-old batter reached 100 off 171 balls, anchoring the innings as Bangladesh faced the West Indies in Sylhet.
details: Towhid Hridoy struck his first Test century to lead Bangladesh's fightback against the West Indies on the third day of the second Test in Sylhet.
Hridoy reached the milestone off 171 balls, hitting 11 fours and a six. He remained unbeaten on 100 at the lunch interval on Saturday.
The 24-year-old showed immense resilience, holding the innings together despite losing four partners during the morning session.
Bangladesh went to lunch at 205-7 after 69 overs, still trailing the West Indies' first-innings total of 356 by 151 runs.
Hridoy's effort followed a tough morning where Mushfiqur Rahim fell for 34 and Litton Das was dismissed for eight.
Mehidy Hasan Miraz contributed 16 runs in a 41-run partnership with Hridoy before being caught off Roston Chase.
The Tigers were already disadvantaged after opener Shadman Islam was ruled out of the first innings due to an ankle injury suffered on Friday.
West Indies currently lead the two-match series 1-0, having posted 356 in their first innings with Amir Jangoo scoring 133.

headline_marked: 229 wickets in 64 Tests: [[Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket]]
headline: 229 wickets in 64 Tests: Mohammed Shami retires from Test cricket
summary: The 36-year-old Indian pacer ends his 13-year red-ball career but confirms he will continue playing white-ball cricket and domestic matches.
details: India fast bowler Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing an end to a distinguished 13-year red-ball career.
The 36-year-old pacer took 229 wickets in 64 Test matches after making his debut against the West Indies in 2013.
Shami shared the news via a social media video posted on the anniversary of his first Test appearance, stating, 'I started it today, and I am ending it today.'
Despite retiring from the longest format, Shami confirmed he remains available for white-ball cricket, including the IPL and domestic limited-overs matches.
He also noted that he would continue to play domestic multi-day cricket if required for his fitness and recovery.
His final Test appearance for India was in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia.
Shami holds the record as India's all-time leading wicket-taker in 50-over World Cups, having claimed 55 wickets in the tournament.
He currently represents Bengal in domestic cricket and plays for the Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League.
caption:
229 Test wickets and a legendary 13-year journey. Mohammed Shami bids farewell to the longest format of the game.

India fast bowler Mohammed Shami has announced his retirement from Test cricket, bringing an end to a distinguished 13-year red-ball career.

The 36-year-old pacer took 229 wickets in 64 Test matches after making his debut against the West Indies in 2013.

Shami shared the news via a social media video posted on the anniversary of his first Test appearance, stating, 'I started it today, and I am ending it today.'

Despite retiring from the longest format, Shami confirmed he remains available for white-ball cricket, including the IPL and domestic limited-overs matches.

He also noted that he would continue to play domestic multi-day cricket if required for his fitness and recovery.

His final Test appearance for India was in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia.

Shami holds the record as India's all-time leading wicket-taker in 50-over World Cups, having claimed 55 wickets in the tournament.

He currently represents Bengal in domestic cricket and plays for the Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League.
